answers.children: Whippets are moderately good with children. Their gentle and affectionate nature suits older calmer youngsters who avoid roughhousing, while the breed's slender build and thin skin leave them vulnerable to accidental injury from boisterous play; originally bred for coursing, their sudden bursts of speed can startle toddlers. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Whippets do not always get along with other pets. High prey drive makes them likely to chase cats and small animals, and their sighthound heritage means they may view anything that runs as quarry, although they can coexist peacefully with dogs raised alongside them.
answers.exercise: Whippets need two twenty-minute sessions of high-intensity running daily. As sprinters rather than endurance athletes this breed requires short bursts at full speed in a securely fenced area or on a lure course; without it their calm indoor couch-potato tendencies give way to restlessness and destructive zooming. Their exceptional speed and agility stem from their history as the poor man's racehorse.
answers.shedding: No — Whippets shed lightly year-round. Their short smooth single coat produces minimal loose hair that is easy to wipe away, so the house stays relatively clean, yet the lack of undercoat also explains their sensitivity to cold and need for a jumper in winter.
answers.hypoallergenic: Whippets have a short smooth coat that sheds minimally and produces little dander indoors. Their low-maintenance coat needs almost no brushing and stays clean without trapping debris from outdoor runs after rabbits. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic yet Whippets are sometimes suggested to allergy sufferers because of the minimal shedding.
answers.training: Whippets are moderately easy to train. Their sensitivity rewards patient gentle methods but the breed's independence and strong prey drive, inherited from its coursing and racing past, can make recall difficult once the Whippet spots movement; they respond best to short positive sessions that respect their intelligence.
answers.lifespan: Whippets live 12-15 years. Their lean muscular build and lack of heavy substance contribute to this range, as does the generally sound health typical of a breed developed for speed by working-class English families who needed hardy companions that could race without frequent veterinary bills.
answers.size: Adult Whippets weigh 25-40 lb and stand 18-22 in at the shoulder. The breed's sleek proportions and light bone give an impression of fragility despite surprising muscle, so they feel compact and unobtrusive in the home while still delivering the startling acceleration that made them weekend racers for coal miners.
answers.barking: Whippets do not bark much. Bred for quiet efficiency during rabbit coursing they remain one of the quietest hounds, offering only an occasional sharp yap when something genuinely warrants attention rather than filling the air with noise like more vocal breeds.
answers.apartment: Yes — Whippets can live in an apartment. Their calm indoor demeanor and low barking suit small homes, while short bursts of sprint exercise can be met with lure games or park visits; the breed's original purpose in cramped miners' terraces confirms they settle quickly after activity.
answers.first-time: Whippets are not the easiest choice for first-time owners. Their sensitive nature and high prey drive demand consistent gentle handling and secure fencing, while the need to manage separation anxiety and provide sprint outlets can overwhelm novices despite the low-maintenance coat and affectionate temperament.
